questions.def: Use 'a' before singular, countable nouns starting with a consonant sound.
questions.question: I want to buy ___ new car.

questions.def: Use 'an' before singular, countable nouns starting with a vowel sound.
questions.question: He is ___ honest man.

questions.def: Use 'the' when referring to a specific store in mind.
questions.question: She went to ___ store to buy milk.

questions.def: Use 'the' before ordinal numbers (first, second, main, etc.).
questions.question: They live on ___ main street.

questions.def: Use 'the' before musical instruments.
questions.question: He likes to play ___ guitar.

questions.def: Use 'the' to refer to a specific, known beach.
questions.question: I am going to ___ beach tomorrow.

questions.def: Use 'a' to introduce a profession or role.
questions.question: She is ___ teacher at the school.

questions.def: Use 'the' before superlatives (tallest, best, etc.).
questions.question: He is ___ tallest boy in class.

questions.def: Use 'an' before adjectives starting with a vowel sound.
questions.question: I read ___ interesting book yesterday.

questions.def: Use 'a' before 'university' because it sounds like 'you'.
questions.question: She is ___ university student.

questions.def: Use 'an' before words starting with a vowel sound.
questions.question: He wants to be ___ engineer.

questions.def: Use 'a' in exclamations about singular nouns.
questions.question: What ___ beautiful day!

questions.def: Do not use an article before uncountable nouns in general.
questions.question: She likes to drink ___ tea in the morning.

questions.def: Use 'the' before plural nouns referring to specific places.
questions.question: They went to ___ mountains last year.

questions.def: Do not use articles before names of academic subjects.
questions.question: He is studying ___ history.

questions.def: Use 'a' because 'European' starts with a consonant sound.
questions.question: She is ___ European woman.

questions.def: You cannot use 'a' before a verb; remove the article.
questions.question: I want a go to the park this afternoon.

questions.def: Use 'the' before 'only' when it modifies a noun.
questions.question: He is a only person who can help.

questions.def: It should be 'a good student', not 'the good student' in this context.
questions.question: She is the good student in the class.

questions.def: Omit the article before 'music' when referring to music in general.
questions.question: I like to listen a music in the evening.

questions.def: It should be 'the United States of America'.
questions.question: They live in a United States of America.

questions.def: If it's HIS hospital, use 'the hospital'.
questions.question: He went to a hospital to visit his friend.

questions.def: Use 'a' before 'very' + adjective + noun: 'a very nice person'.
questions.question: She is the very nice person I know.

questions.def: Use 'an' before apple, and 'eats' for singular he/she/it.
questions.question: He ___ apple every day.

questions.def: She goes to the school.
questions.question: She ___ to ___ school.

questions.def: Use 'the' before musical instruments.
questions.question: He likes to ___ ___ piano.

questions.def: Use 'the' before 'only'.
questions.question: She is ___ only child in her family.

questions.def: Use 'an' because 'idea' starts with a vowel sound.
questions.question: I ___ idea.

questions.def: Omit the article before 'lunch'.
questions.question: We ___ lunch.

questions.def: Use 'the' before landmarks.
questions.question: They ___ Eiffel Tower.
